headline: Highest risk is AutoGen’s broad code-execution and filesystem/network defaults; the paired content-writing repo adds little direct interaction risk but can amplify misuse if its outputs are treated as instructions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest tool calls and code execution per agent role, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a non-runnable content repo with no shared channel or parser surface. The pair lacks a documented direct bridge, so prompt injection is only plausible through unusual manual copy/paste or external orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from agent_b into agent_a prompts or tool inputs
IF a separate orchestrator bridges agent_b text into agent_a without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only and outside agent_a prompt inputs
Add a provenance tag to any copied text before feeding agent_a
Use a separate review step for any instructions extracted from agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce content-to-instruction filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model provider API keys, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering has no declared data classes or I/O surfaces. No shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented, so leakage is not evidenced; the main risk is accidental copying of sensitive application data into agent_a outputs.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is pasted into agent_a prompts or files
IF agent_a outputs are exported into agent_b-derived documentation or notes
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in agent_a working directories
Redact application data before any manual transfer
Store agent_a outputs in a separate folder from agent_b materials
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on copied text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited to unusual shared directories or external wrappers not documented here.
conditions: IF both are configured to write into the same working directory
IF an external orchestrator gives agent_b a mutable workspace not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable writes for agent_b-side documentation workflows
Run agent_a in Docker or another isolated executor
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for any shared workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code and actions from role-played agents, and Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-content repository that could be used as source material. If agent_a’s output is treated as authoritative by downstream workflows, agent_b can amplify unverified instructions; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b-derived prompts or runbooks without review
IF downstream automation executes actions based on agent_a-generated text
mitigations: Require human review before acting on agent_a outputs
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts
Separate generation from execution steps
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking tool

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and application data, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a public content repo with no declared regulated-data handling. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive data in agent_a workflows; agent_b is not cited for a specific regulated-data duty.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into agent_a workflows
IF outputs derived from agent_a are published through agent_b materials
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_a prompts and files
Review any publication workflow before sharing outputs
Use a separate non-sensitive test dataset
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
